grades.quote: When an SRET instruction is executed, SIE is set to SPIE, then SPIE is set to 1.
grades.reason: Directly explains SRET’s privilege restoration using SPP, interrupt-enable restoration using SPIE, and subsequent SPP/SPIE updates.

grades.quote: kernelvec pops the saved registers from the stack and executes sret, which copies sepc to pc and resumes the interrupted kernel code.
grades.reason: Identifies SRET’s restoration of the program counter from sepc; the general-register restoration described is performed by software.
Provides navigation to relevant architectural registers, but no SRET state-change semantics.

grades.quote: When executing an _`x`_ `RET` instruction, if the new privilege mode is `y` , then `ELP` is set to the value of _`x`_ `PELP` if _`y`_ `LPE` (see Section 22.1.1) is 1; otherwise, it is set to `NO_LP_EXPECTED` ; _`x`_ `PELP` is set to `NO_LP_EXPECTED` .
grades.reason: Explains conditional restoration of extension-specific landing-pad state on SRET, a useful subset of its architectural state changes.
